allies.rationale_text: Incentives explain why nominal authority can lose to the actor controlling the operational payoff, the next move, or the real fallback lane.
allies.source_quote: Power Dynamics works best in combination with models that clarify incentives
allies.affinity_rationale: Complementary framing — 'together they explain why formal authority often loses' — but not described as the primary or essential mechanism for power-dynamics analysis.
allies.activation_condition: When mapping which party controls the operational payoff, the next move, or the real outside option in a power relationship

allies.rationale_text: Lock-in clarifies how integration, retraining, and dependency costs narrow the future option set and invert leverage after commitment.
allies.source_quote: Lock In explains how commitment changes the future option set
allies.affinity_rationale: Directly feeds the model's core mechanism — lock-in drives leverage inversion, one of power-dynamics' key heuristics ('Track leverage inversion over time'), with a concrete example of buyer losing leverage after migration.
allies.activation_condition: When analyzing negotiations or partnerships where commitment costs are asymmetric and leverage may invert after integration or migration

allies.rationale_text: Optionality strengthens power-dynamics analysis by preserving live fallback paths and reversible exits before leverage collapses.
allies.source_quote: preserve leverage by keeping a live fallback lane and a reversible exit path
allies.affinity_rationale: Described as 'strengthening' power-dynamics analysis — useful tactical complement for preserving fallback lanes, but extracted from strengths section rather than the explicit ally table.
allies.activation_condition: When designing strategies to preserve fallback lanes and reversible exit paths before leverage consolidates with one party

antagonists.rationale_text: Confirmation-bias distorts power-dynamics by making teams see the leverage structure they want rather than the outside option they actually have.
antagonists.source_quote: Teams often see the leverage structure they want to see
antagonists.affinity_rationale: Directly distorts the core leverage analysis — makes teams see the leverage structure they want rather than the outside option evidence actually supports.
antagonists.activation_condition: When assessing relative bargaining position and the team's evidence for its outside option has not been independently tested

antagonists.rationale_text: Opportunity-cost counters power-dynamics tunnel vision by asking whether winning the negotiation is even worth pursuing relative to better alternatives.
antagonists.source_quote: over-focus on winning the negotiation instead of asking whether the game is worth playing relative to better alternatives
antagonists.affinity_rationale: Broader perspective correction — asks whether winning the negotiation is worth pursuing relative to better alternatives, rather than targeting the leverage analysis itself.
antagonists.activation_condition: When teams are deeply invested in winning a specific negotiation without comparing to the value of their next-best alternative

structured_tensions.tension_text: Power-dynamics conflicts with confirmation-bias when a team keeps acting as if its outside option is stronger than the evidence supports.
structured_tensions.source_quote: A buyer keeps acting as if the supplier needs the deal more, even after capacity signals and fallback evidence say otherwise.

curation_notes.summary: Layer 1+2 enrichment complete. Allies: lock-in 0.90 (strong — drives leverage inversion mechanism), incentives 0.80 (moderate — foundational context), optionality 0.80 (moderate — tactical fallback preservation). Antagonists differentiated: confirmation-bias 0.90 (strong — distorts leverage perception), opportunity-cost 0.80 (moderate — broader perspective). Activation conditions assigned to all allies and antagonists.
donor_drops: Did not preserve broader game-theory or information-asymmetry expansion because the current vocabulary already supports a cleaner leverage surface.
open_questions: The source also names principal-agent-problem, but the kept ally set favors the more operational leverage and reversibility neighborhood.
